technical_findings: Correct chain-rule formula; ratio factorization is not universally defined when inner increment is zero. Remainder proof repairs this without requiring nonzero derivative or one-to-one inner function.
Differentiability at inner/base points and nearby composition domain required; differentiability of inner ensures continuity.
Sine/square order changes expression; general noncommutativity does not prohibit commuting pairs.
cos(1/x) and x^(-n) require x nonzero; negative-integer power proof uses n positive integer.
Radians for trig derivatives. Higher derivatives require successive existence.
D^n x^n=n! for n positive integer by positive-integer power rule, repeated constant-factor rule and induction.
